earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 a3q26exhibit991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 SCHWAB DELIVERS RECORD NET NEW ASSETS & EARNINGS Record Quarterly Core Net New Assets of $190.4 Billion, Up 38% Year-Over-Year 3Q Net Revenues Reached a Record $7.2 Billion, Up 17% Year-Over-Year Record GAAP Earnings Per Share of $1.62; $1.69 Adjusted (1) – Up 29% versus 3Q25 WESTLAKE, Texas, October 15, 2026 – The Charles Schwab Corporation reported net income for the third quarter totaling $2.9 billion, or earnings per share of $1.62. Excluding $151 million of pre-tax transaction-related costs, adjusted (1) net income and earnings per share equaled $3.0 billion and $1.69, respectively. Client Driven Growth $190.4B 3Q26 Core Net New Assets “During the third quarter, clients opened 1.2 million new brokerage accounts and entrusted Schwab with $190.4 billion in core net new assets – an annualized growth rate of 5.8%. We are delivering new capabilities and solutions, while our leading value proposition continues to resonate with investors and RIAs.” President & CEO Rick Wurster Deepen Client Relationships 55% 3Q26 Schwab Wealth Advisory TM Net Flows Growth vs. 3Q25 “As investing plays an increasingly central role in people’s financial lives, clients continue to turn to Schwab for our broad set of wealth, trading, and banking capabilities. During the quarter, Pledged Asset Line TM balances grew to $37.3 billion, up 59% year-over-year, while net flows into Schwab Wealth Advisory TM increased 55%.” President & CEO Rick Wurster Diversified Revenue Growth 17% 3Q26 Revenue Growth vs. 3Q25 “Deeper client engagement across Schwab's platform continues to broaden and strengthen our revenue model, helping our third quarter revenue increase 17% year-over-year to a record $7.2 billion.” CFO Mike Verdeschi Strong Earnings Momentum 29% 3Q26 GAAP EPS Growth vs. 3Q25 “Our diversified business model, continued focus on meeting clients’ evolving needs, and industry leading scale combined to drive year-over-year GAAP earnings growth of 29% to a record $1.62, or $1.69 on an adjusted (1) basis.” CFO Mike Verdeschi 3Q26 Client and Business Highlights • Total client assets increased 15% year-over-year to $13.33 trillion • Core net new assets totaled $190.4 billion, up 38% versus 3Q25 • New brokerage account openings equaled 1.2 million, helping bring total client accounts to 48.6 million • Managed Investing Solutions net flows grew 22% versus 3Q25 • Bank loan balances equaled $72.3 billion at September month-end, up 35% year-over-year • Margin loan balances increased 14% quarter-over-quarter to $187.9 billion at quarter-end, including $60.7 billion related to long/short strategies (2) • Daily average trading volume equaled 10.7 million – up 44% versus 3Q25 • Announced Single Stock Futures on the thinkorswim ® trading platform and plans to expand digital assets available in Schwab Crypto TM • Introduced Charley, a new AI-powered assistant that provides U.S. retail clients with conversational access to Schwab’s tools and insights • Partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors directly to the independent RIAs Schwab serves • Schwab was recognized as one of Fortune’s 2026 Most Innovative Companies (3) - All per-share results are rounded to the nearest cent, based on weighted-average diluted common shares outstanding. 3Q26 Financial Commentary • Quarterly net revenues grew year-over-year by 17% to a record $7.2 billion • Net interest margin expanded quarter-over-quarter to 3.04% • Client transactional sweep cash balances ended September at $492.8 billion, an increase of $7.1 billion versus the prior quarter-end, reflecting continued demand for long/short strategies and organic growth, partially offset by client asset allocation decisions • Average interest-earning assets for the quarter equaled $451.5 billion, up 8% versus 3Q25 • Asset management and administration fees grew by 14% year-over-year to $1.9 billion, powered by the firm’s organic growth and investors’ increased utilization of our wealth and asset management solutions • Clients remained engaged with the market, driving trading revenue of $1.2 billion, up 16% year-over-year • GAAP expenses for the quarter increased 9% year-over-year; excluding acquisition and integration-related costs and the amortization of acquired intangibles of $151 million, adjusted total expenses (1) were also up 9% relative to 3Q25 • Capital ratios across the firm remained strong – including preliminary consolidated Tier 1 Leverage and adjusted Tier 1 Leverage (1) of 8.9 % and 7.0 %, respectively • Repurchased 4.7 million shares of our common stock for $0.5 billion during the quarter (1) Further details on non-GAAP financial measures and a reconciliation of such measures to GAAP reported results are included on pages 10-12 of this release. (2) Client margin loans and short credits related to certain long/short strategies utilized by RIAs are excluded from interest-earning assets and company funding sources. (3) Fortune America’s Most Innovative Companies 2026 was given on March 25, 2026, and expires on March 24, 2027. The criteria, evaluation, and ranking were determined by Fortune, partnered with Statista. Visit https://www.fortune.com/ranking/americas-most-innovative-companies/ for more information. Schwab paid a licensing fee to Fortune for use of the award and logos. Fall Business Update The company will host its Fall Business Update for institutional investors this morning from 7:30 a.m. - 8:30 a.m. CT, 8:30 a.m. - 9:30 a.m. ET. Registration for this Update webcast is accessible at https://www.aboutschwab.com/schwabevents . - 2 - Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements relating to the company’s diversified business model, scale, capabilities, solutions, value proposition, and client engagement. These forward-looking statements reflect management’s expectations as of the date hereof. Achievement of these expectations and objectives is subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from the expressed expectations. Important factors that may cause such differences are described in the company’s most recent reports on Form 10-K and Form 10-Q, which have been filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission and are available on the company’s website ( https://www.aboutschwab.com/financial-reports ) and on the Securities and Exchange Commission’s website ( https://www.sec.gov ). The company makes no commitment to update any forward-looking statements. About Charles Schwab The Charles Schwab Corporation (NYSE: SCHW) is a leading provider of financial services, with 40.3 million active brokerage accounts, 5.9 million workplace plan participant accounts, 2.4 million banking accounts, and $13.33 trillion in client assets. Through its operating subsidiaries, the company provides a full range of wealth management, securities brokerage, banking, asset management, custody, and financial advisory services to individual investors and independent investment advisors. Its broker-dealer subsidiary, Charles Schwab & Co., Inc. (member SIPC, https://www.sipc.org ), and its affiliates offer a complete range of investment services and products including an extensive selection of mutual funds; financial planning and investment advice; retirement plan and equity compensation plan services; referrals to independent, fee-based investment advisors; and custodial, operational and trading support for independent, fee-based investment advisors through Schwab Advisor Services TM . Its primary banking subsidiary, Charles Schwab Bank, SSB (member FDIC and an Equal Housing Lender), provides banking and lending services and products. More information is available at https://www.aboutschwab.com .
